label: Market equilibrium
name: demand_supply_equilibrium
intended_use: Equilibrium price and quantity for declared linear demand and supply curves (Qd = a - bP, Qs = c + dP), with consumer and producer surplus.
unsupported_use: Estimating the curves from data; non-linear demand or supply; shifts, dynamics or expectations; taxes, externalities or market power; causal claims.
assumptions: Demand slopes down and supply slopes up, both linearly.
All else equal: no shifts, taxes, externalities or market power.
The curves are the owner's declared functions, not estimated from data.
limitations: Linear curves only; no dynamics, expectations or general equilibrium.
Surplus is geometric area, not a measured welfare change.
No tax, subsidy, price control or externality is included.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, must be positive

inputs.name: supply_slope
inputs.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, must be positive

defaults.question: Curve form
defaults.default_chosen: Quantity-dependent linear curves: Qd = a - bP and Qs = c + dP. If you have P = a - bQ, rearrange it first.
defaults.impact: Using the inverse form without rearranging swaps the slope and gives the wrong equilibrium.

defaults.question: Welfare measure
defaults.default_chosen: Consumer and producer surplus are the geometric areas under the declared linear curves.
defaults.impact: With non-linear curves or externalities these triangles are not the welfare change.

label: Price elasticity of demand
name: elasticity
intended_use: Arc (midpoint) price elasticity of demand between two declared price-quantity observations, with the revenue change and an elastic/inelastic classification.
unsupported_use: Point elasticity at a single price without a demand function; income or cross-price elasticity; estimating elasticity from a regression; causal claims.
assumptions: The two observations lie on the same demand curve.
All else equal: no income, substitute price or taste change between the observations.
The arc formula is the agreed convention for a discrete change.
limitations: Arc elasticity only; no point elasticity without a demand function.
No income, cross-price or supply elasticity.
Two observations cannot identify a demand curve or prove causality.

defaults.question: Elasticity formula
defaults.default_chosen: Arc (midpoint): the percentage change in quantity divided by the percentage change in price, using the average of the two values in each denominator.
defaults.impact: The point formula at one end of the range gives a different number.

defaults.question: Sign
defaults.default_chosen: The signed elasticity is reported; the absolute value is used for the elastic/inelastic classification.
defaults.impact: Reporting a negative number as inelastic is a common error.

label: Tax incidence and deadweight loss
name: tax_incidence
intended_use: Economic incidence of a declared per-unit tax in a linear partial-equilibrium market: consumer and producer prices, the burden split, tax revenue and deadweight loss.
unsupported_use: Estimating the curves; ad valorem taxes; a tax in a non-linear or general-equilibrium model; the statutory incidence; distributional or dynamic effects.
assumptions: Linear demand and supply, all else equal.
The tax is a fixed amount per unit, not a percentage of price.
The market is competitive and partial equilibrium.
limitations: Per-unit tax only; no ad valorem tax.
No income effects, other markets, evasion or administration costs.
The incidence split depends on the declared slopes, not on who hands the tax to the government.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, must be positive

inputs.name: supply_slope
inputs.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, must be positive

defaults.question: Who the tax is levied on
defaults.default_chosen: A per-unit tax on sellers. With the same rate, a tax on buyers gives the same economic incidence.
defaults.impact: The statutory side does not determine who bears the burden.

defaults.question: Welfare loss
defaults.default_chosen: Deadweight loss is the triangle between the declared linear demand and supply curves over the fall in quantity.
defaults.impact: Non-linear curves or other market effects change the loss.

label: Price ceilings and floors
name: price_control
intended_use: The effect of a declared price ceiling or floor on a linear competitive market: quantity traded, shortage or surplus, and deadweight loss.
unsupported_use: Estimating the curves; rationing, queues or black markets; quality changes; dynamic or general-equilibrium effects; a control that is not a single fixed price.
assumptions: Linear demand and supply, all else equal.
The control is a single fixed price that is enforced.
The market is competitive and partial equilibrium.
limitations: No rationing, queues, black markets or quality adjustment.
No dynamics or general-equilibrium effects.
Deadweight loss is the triangle between the declared linear curves.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, must be positive

inputs.name: supply_slope
inputs.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, must be positive

defaults.question: Binding test
defaults.default_chosen: A ceiling binds only below the equilibrium price; a floor binds only above it.
defaults.impact: A non-binding control leaves the market at equilibrium.

defaults.question: Quantity traded
defaults.default_chosen: The short side of the market determines quantity traded.
defaults.impact: The long side's notional quantity is reported but not traded.

label: Market concentration (HHI)
name: market_concentration
intended_use: Market concentration from declared firm revenues: Herfindahl-Hirschman index (0-10,000), CR1, CR4 and the equivalent number of equal-sized firms.
unsupported_use: Defining the market; estimating revenues; import competition or geographic markets; merger simulation; applying a threshold as a legal conclusion.
assumptions: The declared revenues cover the relevant market.
Each firm's revenue is its market sales, not total corporate revenue across other markets.
The market boundary is the owner's judgement.
limitations: No market definition, import competition or geographic segmentation.
No merger simulation, entry or dynamic effects.
No legal threshold is applied; any threshold is a convention the user supplies.

inputs.name: firm_revenues
inputs.desc: revenue for each firm; shares are derived from the total

defaults.question: Share scale
defaults.default_chosen: Shares are percentages of total revenue, so the HHI runs from 0 to 10,000.
defaults.impact: Fractions instead of percentages give an HHI from 0 to 1.

defaults.question: Market definition
defaults.default_chosen: The firms and revenues you declare are the market; the tool does not define it for you.
defaults.impact: A different market boundary changes every concentration measure.

label: Cost curves
name: cost_curves
intended_use: Average cost, average variable cost, average fixed cost and marginal cost at a declared quantity for the quadratic cost function TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with optional price, revenue, profit and a shutdown flag.
unsupported_use: Estimating the cost function; step costs, learning curves or capacity limits; economies of scope; a full cost-curve schedule.
assumptions: The declared quadratic cost function describes the relevant range.
Fixed cost does not change with quantity.
The quantity is positive.
limitations: One quantity only; no cost schedule across quantities.
No step costs, capacity limits, learning or economies of scope.
The shutdown test assumes the quadratic term is non-negative.

inputs.name: price
inputs.desc: optional price for revenue and profit

inputs.name: quadratic_cost
inputs.desc: quadratic variable cost per unit squared

inputs.name: quantity
inputs.desc: the quantity at which costs are evaluated

defaults.question: Cost function
defaults.default_chosen: TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with non-negative coefficients.
defaults.impact: A different functional form gives different average and marginal costs.

defaults.question: Shutdown test
defaults.default_chosen: The firm shuts down when price is below the linear cost, which is the minimum average variable cost when the quadratic term is non-negative.
defaults.impact: With a negative quadratic term the minimum is not at zero and the test would not apply.

label: Profit maximisation
name: profit_maximization
intended_use: Profit-maximising quantity and price for a firm facing linear demand P = a - bQ and quadratic cost TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with revenue, cost, profit, markup and the Lerner index.
unsupported_use: Estimating demand or cost; multi-product firms; price discrimination; entry, dynamics or strategic interaction; a competitive market price taken as given.
assumptions: The firm faces the declared linear demand curve.
The cost function is quadratic and non-decreasing.
The firm is a single-price monopolist or monopoly-like seller.
limitations: Single product and single period.
No price discrimination, strategic interaction or entry.
The result is arithmetic on the declared curves, not evidence about a real market.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in P = a - bQ, must be positive

defaults.question: Market structure
defaults.default_chosen: A single-price firm facing the declared downward-sloping demand curve; MR = MC.
defaults.impact: A price-taking firm sets price equal to marginal cost instead.

defaults.question: Cost function
defaults.default_chosen: TC = fixed + linear x Q + quadratic x Q squared, with non-negative coefficients.
defaults.impact: A different cost function changes the optimum.

label: Markup and Lerner index
name: market_power
intended_use: Markup and Lerner index from a declared price and marginal cost, with the implied demand elasticity under the single-price monopoly model.
unsupported_use: Estimating marginal cost; proving market power or consumer harm; a dynamic or strategic game; a multi-product firm; a regulated price.
assumptions: The declared marginal cost is the relevant marginal cost.
The firm sets a single price.
The price and cost are from the same period and product.
limitations: Two declared numbers only; no cost estimation.
No legal threshold or competitive assessment is applied.
The implied elasticity is model-conditional.

inputs.name: marginal_cost
inputs.desc: marginal cost at the relevant quantity

defaults.question: What the index means
defaults.default_chosen: The Lerner index is (price - marginal cost) / price; it is a static markup measure.
defaults.impact: A high markup is not by itself evidence of harm or of a legal violation.

defaults.question: Implied elasticity
defaults.default_chosen: Reported only when the Lerner index is positive, as its inverse under the single-price monopoly model.
defaults.impact: With price equal to marginal cost the implied elasticity is undefined.

label: Price discrimination
name: price_discrimination
intended_use: Third-degree price discrimination across two separated linear markets with constant marginal cost: quantities, prices and profit.
unsupported_use: Estimating demand; arbitrage or market separation; first- or second-degree discrimination; menu costs, capacity or welfare comparison with a single price.
assumptions: The two markets are separable and resale is impossible.
Demand is linear and marginal cost is constant.
The firm can set a different price in each market.
limitations: No arbitrage, capacity, menu cost or fixed cost.
No welfare comparison with a single price.
Two markets only.

inputs.name: demand_intercept_1
inputs.desc: intercept of demand in market one

inputs.name: demand_intercept_2
inputs.desc: intercept of demand in market two

inputs.name: demand_slope_1
inputs.desc: positive slope of demand in market one

inputs.name: demand_slope_2
inputs.desc: positive slope of demand in market two

defaults.question: Discrimination
defaults.default_chosen: Third degree: a separate linear price in each market, with no resale.
defaults.impact: If resale is possible the two prices collapse toward one.

defaults.question: Cost
defaults.default_chosen: Constant marginal cost across both markets.
defaults.impact: Different costs or capacity constraints change both prices.

label: Cournot duopoly
name: cournot_duopoly
intended_use: Two-firm Cournot equilibrium with linear demand and constant marginal costs: quantities, price and profits.
unsupported_use: Estimating demand or costs; more than two firms; capacity, product differentiation, repeated interaction or collusion; a firm priced out of the market.
assumptions: Two firms, homogeneous products and linear demand.
Constant marginal costs.
Simultaneous quantity choice and no collusion.
limitations: Two firms only; no entry, capacity or differentiation.
One-shot game; no repeated interaction or collusion.
A corner solution is refused.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in P = a - bQ, positive

inputs.name: marginal_cost_1
inputs.desc: constant marginal cost of firm one

inputs.name: marginal_cost_2
inputs.desc: constant marginal cost of firm two

defaults.question: Competition
defaults.default_chosen: One-shot quantity competition with simultaneous choices.
defaults.impact: Bertrand price competition or Stackelberg leadership gives a different outcome.

defaults.question: Equilibrium
defaults.default_chosen: Interior Cournot equilibrium; a firm priced out of the market is refused.
defaults.impact: A corner solution would need a different model.

label: Nash equilibrium (2x2)
name: nash_equilibrium
intended_use: Pure-strategy Nash equilibria of a declared 2x2 game, with a flag for each cell and the number of equilibria.
unsupported_use: Mixed strategies; games larger than 2x2; sequential or repeated games; coalitional games; selecting among multiple equilibria.
assumptions: The payoffs are the players' utilities and are comparable only within each player.
The game is one-shot and simultaneous.
Each player knows the payoff matrix.
limitations: Pure strategies only; mixed equilibria are not computed.
2x2 games only.
Multiple equilibria are reported, not ranked.

inputs.name: column_payoffs
inputs.desc: column player's payoffs in the same cell order

inputs.name: row_payoffs
inputs.desc: row player's payoffs in the order (row one, column one), (row one, column two), (row two, column one), (row two, column two)

defaults.question: Strategies
defaults.default_chosen: Two players, two pure strategies each, simultaneous moves.
defaults.impact: Mixed or sequential strategies are a different solution concept.

defaults.question: Ties
defaults.default_chosen: A cell where neither player can gain by a unilateral switch is counted as a weak Nash equilibrium.
defaults.impact: A strict-equilibrium-only rule could report fewer cells.

label: Panel fixed effects
name: panel_regression
intended_use: Balanced-panel fixed-effects (within) slope and intercept for one regressor, with within R-squared and degrees of freedom.
unsupported_use: Unbalanced panels; time-invariant regressors; dynamic panels with lagged outcomes; clustered or robust standard errors; causal claims.
assumptions: The panel is balanced and the entity effect is additive.
The slope is common across entities.
No time-varying omitted variable is correlated with x.
limitations: Time-invariant regressors are absorbed and cannot be estimated.
No standard errors, clustering or robust inference.
Dynamic panel bias is not addressed.

inputs.name: data
inputs.desc: one record per entity-period; the panel must be balanced

defaults.question: Estimator
defaults.default_chosen: Within (fixed-effects) transformation, which removes each entity's mean.
defaults.impact: Random effects or pooled OLS would use between-entity variation and give a different slope.

defaults.question: Inference
defaults.default_chosen: No standard errors are computed; the output is the point estimate and within fit.
defaults.impact: Clustered or robust inference would need a declared design.

label: Instrumental variables
name: instrumental_variables
intended_use: Just-identified instrumental-variables slope and intercept with one endogenous regressor and one excluded instrument, plus the first-stage and OLS slopes for comparison.
unsupported_use: Over-identified models; weak instruments; controls; robust or clustered inference; testing the exclusion restriction; causal claims without a defended design.
assumptions: The instrument is relevant and satisfies the exclusion restriction.
The relationship is linear with a constant effect.
Observations are independent.
limitations: One instrument and one endogenous regressor only.
No weak-instrument diagnostics or over-identification test.
No controls, robust or clustered standard errors.

defaults.question: Estimator
defaults.default_chosen: Just-identified 2SLS, which here reduces to cov(z, y) / cov(z, x).
defaults.impact: Over-identification or controls would need a matrix estimator.

defaults.question: Instrument validity
defaults.default_chosen: Relevance is checked by a non-zero cov(z, x); the exclusion restriction is assumed, not tested.
defaults.impact: An invalid instrument gives a biased estimate with no warning.

label: Regression discontinuity
name: regression_discontinuity
intended_use: Sharp regression-discontinuity estimate from a local linear fit on each side of a declared cutoff and bandwidth.
unsupported_use: Fuzzy designs; manipulation of the running variable; optimal bandwidth selection; covariates; bias-corrected or robust inference; causal claims without a defended design.
assumptions: Treatment is determined by the running variable crossing the cutoff.
No manipulation of the running variable.
No other discontinuity at the cutoff.
limitations: No optimal bandwidth, bias correction or covariates.
Sharp design only; no fuzzy RDD.
No robust or clustered inference.

inputs.name: bandwidth
inputs.desc: the symmetric bandwidth around the cutoff

inputs.name: data
inputs.desc: one record per observation: the running variable and the outcome

defaults.question: Fit
defaults.default_chosen: A separate local linear fit on each side, with the estimate as the jump in intercepts at the cutoff.
defaults.impact: A global polynomial or a different bandwidth gives a different estimate.

defaults.question: Design
defaults.default_chosen: Sharp design: treatment switches exactly at the cutoff.
defaults.impact: A fuzzy design would need an instrument for treatment.

label: Probit model
name: probit
intended_use: Binary probit with one predictor: latent-index coefficients, log likelihood, McFadden pseudo R-squared and the marginal effect at the mean.
unsupported_use: Multiple predictors, interactions, robust or clustered inference, separation, causal claims, or predicted probabilities outside the observed support.
assumptions: The outcome is binary and observations are independent.
The latent index is linear in the predictor.
No separation or near-separation.
limitations: One predictor only; no controls or interactions.
No robust, clustered or bootstrapped standard errors.
Separation is refused rather than penalised.

inputs.name: x
inputs.desc: the numeric predictor, same length as y

defaults.question: Estimator
defaults.default_chosen: Maximum likelihood by Newton-Raphson on the probit likelihood.
defaults.impact: Logit or a linear probability model gives different coefficients.

defaults.question: Marginal effect
defaults.default_chosen: Reported at the mean of the predictor; it is not a constant effect.
defaults.impact: A marginal effect at a different x changes the number.

label: GDP and national income
name: national_income
intended_use: GDP by the expenditure approach, plus GNP, NNP, net exports, optional GDP per capita and optional real GDP from a declared deflator.
unsupported_use: Retrieving national-accounts data; the income or production approach; double-counting checks; chain-linked or base-year rebasing; informal or underground activity.
assumptions: The components are one period's declared values in one currency.
Imports are already included in the other components and are subtracted once.
The deflator, if used, is an index with a base of 100.
limitations: No income-approach or production-approach cross-check.
No base-year conversion, chain-linking or seasonal adjustment.
No informal-sector, underground or home-production adjustment.

inputs.name: gdp_deflator
inputs.desc: optional GDP deflator index (base 100) for real GDP

inputs.name: net_factor_income
inputs.desc: net factor income from abroad, default 0

inputs.name: population
inputs.desc: optional population for GDP per capita

defaults.question: GDP approach
defaults.default_chosen: Expenditure approach: C + I + G + X - M from the declared components.
defaults.impact: The income and production approaches would need different data and can differ in practice.

defaults.question: Real GDP
defaults.default_chosen: Real GDP is nominal GDP divided by the declared deflator index divided by one hundred.
defaults.impact: A different base year or chain-linking convention gives a different real series.

label: Growth rate and CAGR
name: growth_rate
intended_use: Total growth, compound annual growth rate and the rule-of-72 doubling time between two declared values, with optional per-capita growth.
unsupported_use: Forecasting future growth; fitting a trend; inflation adjustment; a growth-accounting decomposition into capital, labour and productivity.
assumptions: The two values are measured on the same basis and currency.
The periods are equal in length.
No inflation adjustment is made unless the values are already real.
limitations: Two observations only; no trend or volatility.
The rule of 72 is approximate.
No growth-accounting decomposition.

inputs.name: periods
inputs.desc: the number of periods between the two values

inputs.name: population_end
inputs.desc: optional ending population for per-capita growth

inputs.name: population_start
inputs.desc: optional starting population for per-capita growth

defaults.question: Growth convention
defaults.default_chosen: CAGR is the constant rate that compounds the start value to the end value over the declared periods.
defaults.impact: A simple average of yearly growth rates gives a different number.

defaults.question: Doubling time
defaults.default_chosen: The rule of 72 is an approximation; the exact time is ln(2)/ln(1 + CAGR).
defaults.impact: The approximation is close only for moderate rates.

label: Inflation and real interest
name: inflation_cpi
intended_use: Inflation from two CPI values, the exact and approximate real interest rate, and optional real wage growth.
unsupported_use: Retrieving CPI data; choosing or rebasing the basket; core versus headline inflation; expectations; a household-specific cost-of-living index.
assumptions: The two CPI values use the same basket and base.
The nominal rate and the CPI cover the same period.
Wages, if used, are nominal values for the same period.
limitations: Two CPI values only; no index construction or rebasing.
No expectations, core measure or household-specific basket.
Real wage growth is an index comparison, not a full cost-of-living measure.

inputs.name: wage_end
inputs.desc: optional nominal wage at the end

inputs.name: wage_start
inputs.desc: optional nominal wage at the start

defaults.question: Inflation measure
defaults.default_chosen: The percentage change in the declared CPI between the two periods.
defaults.impact: A different basket, base period or core measure gives a different rate.

defaults.question: Real interest
defaults.default_chosen: Exact Fisher relation; the nominal-minus-inflation figure is reported only as an approximation.
defaults.impact: At high inflation the approximation can be far from the exact rate.

label: Unemployment and participation
name: unemployment_rate
intended_use: Unemployment rate, labour-force participation rate and employment-population ratio from declared labour-force, employment and working-age population counts.
unsupported_use: Retrieving labour-market data; defining who is in the labour force; underemployment, discouragement or informal work; seasonal adjustment.
assumptions: The three counts cover the same population and period.
The labour force does not exceed the working-age population.
The employed are a subset of the labour force.
limitations: Counts only; no underemployment or informal-sector adjustment.
No seasonal adjustment or demographic standardisation.
The labour-force definition is the owner's.

inputs.name: labour_force
inputs.desc: the labour force: employed plus unemployed

defaults.question: Labour-force definition
defaults.default_chosen: The labour force is exactly the count you declare; discouraged workers outside it are not counted.
defaults.impact: A broader definition that includes discouraged workers would raise the unemployment rate.

defaults.question: Denominators
defaults.default_chosen: The unemployment rate uses the labour force; participation and employment ratios use the working-age population.
defaults.impact: Mixing the denominators gives a different and usually misleading rate.

label: Money multiplier
name: money_multiplier
intended_use: Simple and currency-adjusted money multipliers from the monetary base, reserve ratio and optional currency drain, with the implied money supply.
unsupported_use: Retrieving monetary aggregates; excess reserves, bank capital or liquidity constraints; central-bank reaction functions; a full money-market model.
assumptions: The reserve ratio is binding and constant.
Banks lend all available funds above reserves.
The currency drain is a constant fraction of deposits.
limitations: No excess reserves, capital or liquidity constraints.
No central-bank policy reaction or interest rate.
The multiplier is an identity, not a forecast.

inputs.name: currency_drain_ratio
inputs.desc: currency held outside banks as a fraction of deposits, default 0

inputs.name: reserve_ratio
inputs.desc: the reserve requirement as a fraction, greater than zero and at most one

defaults.question: Reserve behaviour
defaults.default_chosen: Banks hold exactly the declared reserve ratio and no excess reserves.
defaults.impact: Excess reserves lower the realised multiplier.

defaults.question: Currency drain
defaults.default_chosen: The simple multiplier assumes no currency drain; the extended multiplier adds the declared drain.
defaults.impact: A positive drain lowers the multiplier.

label: Fiscal multipliers
name: fiscal_multiplier
intended_use: Government-spending, tax and balanced-budget multipliers from a declared marginal propensity to consume and proportional tax rate, with the output change from declared fiscal changes.
unsupported_use: Estimating the mpc or tax rate; crowding out, confidence, supply-side effects, lags, open-economy leakages or a full macro model.
assumptions: The mpc and tax rate are constant over the relevant range.
Prices and interest rates do not respond.
There is spare capacity.
limitations: No crowding out, confidence, supply-side or open-economy effects.
No lags or expectations.
The multipliers are arithmetic identities, not estimated policy effects.

inputs.name: mpc
inputs.desc: marginal propensity to consume, between zero and one

defaults.question: Model
defaults.default_chosen: Closed-economy Keynesian multiplier with a proportional income tax.
defaults.impact: An open economy or a price-level response gives a smaller multiplier.

defaults.question: Tax change
defaults.default_chosen: A lump-sum tax change uses the same tax multiplier on the declared change.
defaults.impact: A proportional tax change is already in the denominator and is a different experiment.

label: Budget balance and debt
name: budget_debt
intended_use: Overall and primary budget balances, the debt-to-GDP ratio, the interest rate and the standard debt-ratio change from declared budget aggregates.
unsupported_use: Forecasting debt; contingent liabilities, off-budget items, currency composition or maturity structure; a full debt-sustainability model; choosing a fiscal rule.
assumptions: The aggregates are one period's declared values in one currency.
The debt stock is at the start of the period.
The interest rate is interest paid divided by the debt stock.
limitations: No contingent liabilities, off-budget items or debt composition.
No forecast path or stochastic stress test.
The debt-ratio change is an identity, not a sustainability verdict.

inputs.name: debt_stock
inputs.desc: the debt stock at the start of the period

inputs.name: inflation_rate
inputs.desc: optional inflation rate for the real interest rate

defaults.question: What spending includes
defaults.default_chosen: government_spending is primary spending and excludes interest; total spending adds interest.
defaults.impact: Including interest in spending would double-count it in the overall balance.

defaults.question: Debt dynamics
defaults.default_chosen: The debt-ratio change is (interest rate - nominal growth) x debt ratio - primary balance ratio, with the declared rates held constant.
defaults.impact: A different growth or interest assumption changes the path.

label: Output gap and Okun's law
name: output_gap_okun
intended_use: Output gap from actual and potential GDP, with the predicted unemployment change from a declared Okun coefficient.
unsupported_use: Estimating potential output; estimating the Okun coefficient; a structural model of the labour market; a forecast.
assumptions: Actual and potential GDP are on the same price and currency basis.
The Okun relation is linear over the relevant range.
The coefficient is the owner's declared value.
limitations: Potential output is declared, not estimated.
The Okun coefficient is not estimated here.
The predicted change is an illustration, not a forecast.

inputs.name: current_unemployment_rate
inputs.desc: current unemployment rate as a fraction, default 0

inputs.name: okun_coefficient
inputs.desc: percentage-point unemployment change per one percent output gap, default 0.5

inputs.name: potential_gdp
inputs.desc: potential GDP on the same basis

defaults.question: Potential output
defaults.default_chosen: Potential GDP is the value you declare; it is not estimated.
defaults.impact: A different potential-output estimate changes the gap.

defaults.question: Okun coefficient
defaults.default_chosen: The coefficient is the owner's declared value, default 0.5 percentage points per one percent gap.
defaults.impact: Different countries and periods have different coefficients.

label: Externalities and Pigouvian tax
name: externality_pigouvian
intended_use: Market and social optimum under a declared per-unit external cost, with the Pigouvian tax and deadweight loss.
unsupported_use: Estimating external damages; valuing non-monetary effects; abatement technology; tax interaction; general-equilibrium or distributional effects.
assumptions: Linear private demand and supply; a constant per-unit external cost.
The external cost is known and additively separable.
Partial equilibrium with no other distortions.
limitations: No damage estimation, non-monetary valuation or abatement technology.
No tax interaction, enforcement cost or distributional analysis.
The tax is a declared Pigouvian benchmark, not an observed policy.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, positive

inputs.name: supply_slope
inputs.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, positive

defaults.question: External cost
defaults.default_chosen: A constant per-unit external cost added to private supply at the social optimum.
defaults.impact: A non-linear or production-dependent damage function gives a different tax.

defaults.question: Policy
defaults.default_chosen: The Pigouvian tax equals the marginal external cost at the optimum.
defaults.impact: A second-best tax in a distorted economy would differ.

label: Public goods
name: public_good
intended_use: Efficient provision of a public good from two declared linear marginal-benefit schedules and one marginal-cost schedule, with total and net benefit.
unsupported_use: Estimating benefits; free-riding games; contribution mechanisms; crowding out; distributional weights; more than two individuals.
assumptions: Two individuals with declared linear marginal benefits.
The good is non-rival and non-excludable.
Marginal cost is linear and positive.
limitations: Two individuals only; no free-riding or contribution game.
No distributional weights, crowding out or administrative cost.
The benefit schedules are declared, not estimated.

inputs.name: mb1_intercept
inputs.desc: intercept of the first marginal-benefit schedule

inputs.name: mb1_slope
inputs.desc: positive slope of the first marginal-benefit schedule

inputs.name: mb2_intercept
inputs.desc: intercept of the second marginal-benefit schedule

inputs.name: mb2_slope
inputs.desc: positive slope of the second marginal-benefit schedule

defaults.question: Aggregation
defaults.default_chosen: Vertical summation of the two marginal-benefit schedules (the Samuelson condition).
defaults.impact: Horizontal summation would be the private-good case, not the public-good case.

defaults.question: Provision
defaults.default_chosen: The efficient quantity is where summed marginal benefit equals marginal cost.
defaults.impact: A voluntary-contribution equilibrium would generally underprovide.

label: Social welfare functions
name: social_welfare
intended_use: Utilitarian, Rawlsian and Nash social welfare from declared incomes, with the selected welfare function.
unsupported_use: Estimating individual utility; interpersonal comparisons beyond income; equivalence scales; non-income dimensions; a policy recommendation.
assumptions: Incomes are positive and comparable across the people listed.
Income is a sufficient proxy for the welfare argument.
The selected function is the intended ethical criterion.
limitations: No equivalence scales, household composition or non-income dimensions.
No interpersonal utility comparison beyond the declared incomes.
The welfare function is a normative choice.

defaults.question: Utility
defaults.default_chosen: Income is used as the utility argument; no separate utility function is estimated.
defaults.impact: A concave utility function would change the utilitarian ranking.

defaults.question: Welfare function
defaults.default_chosen: The selected function is reported alongside all three; the choice is ethical, not empirical.
defaults.impact: Utilitarian, Rawlsian and Nash can rank the same distribution differently.

label: Gini coefficient
name: gini_coefficient
intended_use: Gini coefficient, mean, minimum and maximum from declared incomes, with the poorest and richest shares.
unsupported_use: Estimating incomes; equivalence scales; taxes and transfers; in-kind income; decomposing inequality by source or group; a policy verdict.
assumptions: Incomes are non-negative and cover the intended population.
Each income belongs to one person or household.
No equivalence scale is applied.
limitations: One summary measure; it hides where in the distribution inequality lies.
No taxes, transfers, in-kind income or equivalence scales.
No decomposition by group or source.

defaults.question: Income definition
defaults.default_chosen: The declared incomes are used as given; the unit and coverage are the owner's choice.
defaults.impact: Pre-tax, post-tax or consumption measures give different Ginis.

defaults.question: Scale
defaults.default_chosen: The Gini is reported between zero and one, not multiplied by one hundred.
defaults.impact: A 0-100 presentation is a scale choice, not a different index.

label: Poverty measures
name: poverty_measures
intended_use: Headcount ratio, poverty gap, squared gap and total shortfall from declared incomes and a declared poverty line.
unsupported_use: Choosing a poverty line; estimating incomes; multidimensional poverty; transient versus chronic poverty; equivalence scales; a policy verdict.
assumptions: Incomes are non-negative and cover the intended population.
The poverty line is fixed and comparable across the observations.
No equivalence scale is applied.
limitations: No multidimensional or transient poverty analysis.
No taxes, transfers, in-kind income or equivalence scales.
The line is a declared choice.

defaults.question: Poverty line
defaults.default_chosen: The line is the owner's declared value; the method does not choose or verify it.
defaults.impact: A higher line raises the headcount and gap.

defaults.question: Gap
defaults.default_chosen: The gap is averaged over the whole population, with a zero shortfall for the non-poor.
defaults.impact: Averaging only over the poor gives a larger number.

label: Tax progressivity
name: tax_progressivity
intended_use: Average tax rate and a simple top-quartile progressivity gap from declared incomes and taxes.
unsupported_use: Estimating taxes; a full Kakwani or Reynolds-Smolensky index; deductions, exemptions or behavioural responses; a policy verdict.
assumptions: Incomes are positive and taxes are non-negative.
The two lists cover the same people and period.
The top quartile is the intended comparison group.
limitations: A simple top-quartile gap, not a full progressivity index.
No deductions, exemptions, incidence or behavioural responses.
No equivalence scale.

inputs.name: taxes
inputs.desc: tax paid, one per income and same length

defaults.question: Progressivity measure
defaults.default_chosen: The gap is the top quartile's tax share minus its income share; positive means the top pays proportionally more.
defaults.impact: A full Kakwani index uses concentration curves and can rank differently.

defaults.question: Top group
defaults.default_chosen: The top quartile by income, with at least one observation.
defaults.impact: A different top group changes the gap.

label: Optimal pollution
name: optimal_pollution
intended_use: Optimal emissions and pollution tax where declared linear marginal damage equals declared linear marginal abatement cost.
unsupported_use: Estimating damage or abatement costs; non-linear or threshold damage; multiple pollutants; technological change; a policy verdict.
assumptions: Linear marginal damage and marginal abatement cost.
One pollutant and one period.
The curves are the owner's declared functions.
limitations: No damage or abatement estimation.
No multiple pollutants, thresholds or technological change.
No distributional or enforcement analysis.

inputs.name: marginal_abatement_slope
inputs.desc: positive slope of marginal abatement cost

defaults.question: Curve form
defaults.default_chosen: Marginal damage rises with emissions and marginal abatement cost falls with emissions, both linearly.
defaults.impact: A non-linear damage function gives a different optimum.

defaults.question: Policy
defaults.default_chosen: The pollution tax equals marginal damage at the optimum.
defaults.impact: A cap-and-trade quantity instrument would need a different model.

label: Comparative advantage
name: comparative_advantage
intended_use: Ricardian comparative advantage from two countries' declared unit labour requirements in two goods, with opportunity costs and specialisation flags.
unsupported_use: Estimating productivity; more than two countries or goods; transport costs, tariffs, demand differences, increasing returns or strategic trade policy.
assumptions: Unit labour requirements are constant and the only input.
Two countries and two goods.
Labour is mobile within a country and immobile between countries.
limitations: No transport costs, tariffs, demand or increasing returns.
Two countries and two goods only.
No distributional analysis of the gains from trade.

inputs.name: countries
inputs.desc: exactly two countries with their unit labour requirements

defaults.question: Trade model
defaults.default_chosen: Two countries, two goods and constant unit labour requirements; the Ricardian textbook case.
defaults.impact: A Heckscher-Ohlin or increasing-returns model gives a different pattern.

defaults.question: Advantage
defaults.default_chosen: Comparative advantage follows the lower opportunity cost, not the lower absolute hours.
defaults.impact: Absolute advantage alone does not determine who should specialise in what.

label: Tariff welfare
name: tariff_welfare
intended_use: Small-country tariff on a linear market: domestic price, imports, tariff revenue and the production and consumption deadweight losses.
unsupported_use: Large-country terms-of-trade effects; retaliation; quotas; transport costs; general-equilibrium or dynamic effects.
assumptions: Linear domestic demand and supply.
The country is a price-taker in world markets.
The tariff is a per-unit amount and is fully enforced.
limitations: Small-country, partial-equilibrium model only.
No retaliation, quota, transport cost or dynamic effect.
No distributional analysis of producers and consumers.

inputs.name: demand_slope
inputs.desc: b in Qd = a - bP, positive

inputs.name: supply_slope
inputs.desc: d in Qs = c + dP, positive

inputs.name: world_price
inputs.desc: the world price before the tariff

defaults.question: Country size
defaults.default_chosen: Small open economy: the world price is taken as given and the tariff is fully passed into the domestic price.
defaults.impact: A large country can shift the world price and gain terms-of-trade.

defaults.question: Welfare
defaults.default_chosen: Production and consumption deadweight-loss triangles plus tariff revenue.
defaults.impact: A quota or a non-linear model gives a different welfare split.

label: Purchasing-power parity
name: exchange_rate_ppp
intended_use: Absolute and relative purchasing-power parity from declared price levels and a nominal exchange rate, with the real rate, misalignment and expected depreciation.
unsupported_use: Retrieving price levels or exchange rates; choosing a basket; non-tradables, transport costs, tariffs or a full equilibrium model.
assumptions: The two price levels cover comparable baskets.
The nominal rate is domestic per foreign.
Relative PPP uses one period and the declared inflation rates.
limitations: No transport costs, tariffs, non-tradables or Balassa-Samuelson effect.
The price levels are declared, not retrieved.
PPP is a long-run benchmark, not a forecast.

inputs.name: domestic_inflation
inputs.desc: optional domestic inflation for relative PPP

inputs.name: foreign_inflation
inputs.desc: optional foreign inflation for relative PPP

inputs.name: nominal_rate
inputs.desc: domestic currency per one unit of foreign currency

inputs.name: price_domestic
inputs.desc: domestic price level or basket cost

inputs.name: price_foreign
inputs.desc: foreign price level in foreign currency

defaults.question: PPP basis
defaults.default_chosen: Absolute PPP on the declared price levels; relative PPP uses the declared inflation rates for one period.
defaults.impact: A different basket or base period gives a different PPP rate.

defaults.question: Real rate
defaults.default_chosen: Real exchange rate = nominal x foreign price / domestic price; 1 means PPP.
defaults.impact: A different quotation convention inverts the real rate.

label: Interest-rate parity
name: interest_rate_parity
intended_use: Covered interest parity: the implied forward rate and forward premium from a spot rate, two interest rates and a declared horizon, with an optional declared forward and real rates.
unsupported_use: Retrieving rates; uncovered parity as a forecast; transaction costs, capital controls, credit or basis risk; a full exchange-rate model.
assumptions: The spot rate is domestic per foreign.
The two interest rates apply to the same horizon.
Capital is mobile and there are no controls or transaction costs.
limitations: No transaction costs, capital controls, credit or basis risk.
Uncovered parity is not a forecast and is not computed.
The forward is implied, not observed, unless declared.

inputs.name: domestic_inflation
inputs.desc: optional domestic inflation for the real rate

inputs.name: domestic_rate
inputs.desc: domestic interest rate for the horizon

inputs.name: foreign_inflation
inputs.desc: optional foreign inflation for the real rate

inputs.name: foreign_rate
inputs.desc: foreign interest rate for the horizon

inputs.name: forward_rate
inputs.desc: optional declared forward rate to compare with parity

inputs.name: spot_rate
inputs.desc: spot domestic currency per foreign currency

defaults.question: Parity
defaults.default_chosen: Covered interest parity with compounding over the declared horizon.
defaults.impact: Simple-interest or continuous compounding gives a slightly different forward.

defaults.question: Forward
defaults.default_chosen: The implied forward is computed; a declared forward is compared with it and the gap is reported.
defaults.impact: A gap can reflect transaction costs, controls or a data mismatch.

label: Balance of payments
name: balance_of_payments
intended_use: Balance-of-payments identity from declared current, capital and financial account balances, with an optional errors term and current-account-to-GDP ratio.
unsupported_use: Retrieving balance-of-payments data; choosing a sign convention; reserve valuation effects; debt-service or sustainability analysis.
assumptions: The three account balances use one sign convention and one period.
Errors and omissions are declared or zero.
GDP, if used, is on the same basis.
limitations: No reserve valuation, debt-service or sustainability analysis.
No decomposition into trade, income and transfers.
The identity does not validate the underlying data.

inputs.name: gdp
inputs.desc: optional nominal GDP for the current-account ratio

defaults.question: Sign convention
defaults.default_chosen: All balances use the same declared sign convention and are added; the method checks the identity, not the convention.
defaults.impact: Mixing conventions can make a balanced position look unbalanced.

defaults.question: Interpretation
defaults.default_chosen: A zero net balance is an accounting identity, not a sustainability verdict.
defaults.impact: A balanced position can still hide risky composition.

label: Human Development Index
name: hdi
intended_use: Human Development Index from declared life expectancy, expected and mean years of schooling and GNI per capita, using the UNDP goalposts.
unsupported_use: Retrieving HDI data; choosing goalposts; inequality-adjusted HDI; multidimensional poverty; a policy verdict.
assumptions: The four inputs are on the UNDP definitions and comparable basis.
The goalposts are the declared UNDP values.
GNI per capita is in purchasing-power terms.
limitations: No inequality adjustment or multidimensional poverty.
The index hides distribution within each dimension.
The data are declared, not retrieved.

inputs.name: gni_per_capita
inputs.desc: GNI per capita in purchasing-power terms

inputs.name: life_expectancy
inputs.desc: life expectancy at birth in years

defaults.question: Goalposts
defaults.default_chosen: UNDP goalposts: life 20-85, expected schooling 0-18, mean schooling 0-15, GNI 100-75,000.
defaults.impact: A different goalpost set gives a different HDI.

defaults.question: Aggregation
defaults.default_chosen: Geometric mean of the three dimension indices.
defaults.impact: An arithmetic mean would be more substitutable across dimensions.

label: Expected utility
name: expected_utility
intended_use: Expected value, expected utility, certainty equivalent and risk premium for a declared gamble under risk neutrality or CRRA utility.
unsupported_use: Estimating utilities or risk aversion; non-expected-utility models; ambiguity; reference dependence (use prospect_theory); a normative recommendation.
assumptions: Probabilities are known and sum to one.
Outcomes are positive final wealth levels.
The utility function and risk aversion are the owner's declared values.
limitations: No probability weighting, ambiguity or reference dependence.
CRRA is defined only for positive outcomes.
The utility parameters are not estimated.

inputs.name: probabilities
inputs.desc: probabilities, same length, summing to one

defaults.question: Utility
defaults.default_chosen: CRRA with the declared risk-aversion coefficient; risk-neutral utility is available as a declared alternative.
defaults.impact: A different utility function changes the certainty equivalent and risk premium.

defaults.question: Outcomes
defaults.default_chosen: Outcomes are final wealth levels and must be positive.
defaults.impact: Gains and losses relative to a reference point belong to prospect_theory, not this method.

label: Prospect theory
name: prospect_theory
intended_use: Kahneman-Tversky-style prospect value from declared outcomes, probabilities and a reference point, with loss aversion, curvature and probability weighting.
unsupported_use: Estimating the parameters; a normative recommendation; ambiguity, framing or reference-point selection; cumulative prospect theory with rank dependence.
assumptions: Outcomes are evaluated relative to the declared reference point.
Probabilities are known and sum to one.
The parameters are the owner's declared values.
limitations: A declared parameterisation, not an estimate.
No cumulative rank-dependent weighting, ambiguity or framing.
Descriptive, not normative.

inputs.name: outcomes
inputs.desc: outcomes to be evaluated relative to the reference

inputs.name: probabilities
inputs.desc: probabilities, same length, summing to one

defaults.question: Value function
defaults.default_chosen: Gains are curved with the gain parameter; losses with the loss parameter and multiplied by loss aversion.
defaults.impact: Different parameters change the prospect value and the ranking of gambles.

defaults.question: Probability weights
defaults.default_chosen: Tversky-Kahneman-style weights, normalised to sum to one.
defaults.impact: Cumulative rank-dependent weighting is not implemented.

label: Real wage and labour market
name: labour_market
intended_use: Real wage, wage share of productivity and optional labour-market tightness from declared nominal wage, CPI, productivity and vacancy/unemployment figures.
unsupported_use: Estimating wages or productivity; hours, composition, taxes, benefits or bargaining; a full labour-market model.
assumptions: The nominal wage, CPI and productivity cover the same period and population.
The CPI is an index with a base of 100.
Productivity is output per worker.
limitations: No hours, composition, taxes, benefits or bargaining.
The wage share is a simple ratio, not a full decomposition.
No regional or sectoral breakdown.

inputs.name: unemployment_rate
inputs.desc: optional unemployment rate as a fraction for tightness

defaults.question: Real wage
defaults.default_chosen: Nominal wage divided by the CPI divided by one hundred.
defaults.impact: A different price index or base year changes the real wage.

defaults.question: Wage share
defaults.default_chosen: Real wage divided by labour productivity, a simple comparison rather than a full labour-share decomposition.
defaults.impact: A full decomposition would need compensation and value-added data.

label: Difference-in-differences
name: difference_in_differences
intended_use: Two-group, two-period difference-in-differences from four declared means.
unsupported_use: Testing parallel trends; covariates, clustering, weights, repeated cross-sections, staggered adoption or a causal claim without the design.
assumptions: The four means are comparable and measured the same way.
The control group would have followed the treated group's trend absent treatment.
No confounding shocks differ between the groups.
limitations: Parallel trends cannot be tested here.
No covariates, clustering, weights or repeated cross-sections.
A two-period, two-group design only.

defaults.question: Design
defaults.default_chosen: Two groups and two periods with declared means.
defaults.impact: A regression with covariates or staggered adoption is a different design.

defaults.question: Identification
defaults.default_chosen: The estimate is causal only under parallel trends, which this method cannot test.
defaults.impact: If trends differ, the estimate is biased.

label: Trend forecast
name: trend_forecast
intended_use: Project a linear trend in a single time series forward for a user-chosen horizon, with prediction intervals and a disclosed out-of-sample error on the recent past.
unsupported_use: Seasonal, cyclical or structural-break series; causal claims; multi-series or driver-based models; long horizons; policy simulations.
assumptions: Observations are in time order with one value per period.
The trend is linear in time.
Errors around the trend are independent and roughly normal.
limitations: No seasonality, cycles, external drivers or structural-break handling.
Extrapolation: the forecast projects the trend beyond the observed range and becomes less reliable the further ahead it goes.
Prediction intervals are approximate in small samples.

inputs.name: horizon
inputs.desc: number of periods ahead to forecast, default 3 (a whole number from 1 to 12)

inputs.name: values
inputs.desc: the time series in period order; blank or null counts as missing at that position

defaults.question: Trend model
defaults.default_chosen: A linear trend in time fitted by ordinary least squares; no seasonality, cycles or external drivers.
defaults.impact: Seasonal or structural-break series will be forecast badly; the out-of-sample check surfaces the recent error.

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: Missing entries keep their position in time and are excluded from the fit; they are not filled in.
defaults.impact: Filling gaps (interpolation) would change the fit.

defaults.question: Prediction intervals
defaults.default_chosen: Classical intervals for the mean forecast plus residual uncertainty, using the t critical value at the declared confidence level.
defaults.impact: They assume independent, roughly normal errors around the trend.

defaults.question: Out-of-sample check
defaults.default_chosen: The last m periods (m is a quarter of the series length, capped at 3) are held out, the trend is refit on the rest, and the mean absolute error and interval coverage on the held-out periods are reported.
defaults.impact: It measures only recent past performance, not future accuracy.

label: Currency conversion
name: currency_convert
intended_use: Convert an amount from one ISO 4217 currency to another at a rate the owner declares, recording the rate, its provenance, any source and date.
unsupported_use: Retrieving or verifying exchange rates; interpolation, forward rates or triangulation; translating a set of statements; multi-currency consolidation; tax or fee conversion.
assumptions: The rate is the owner's declaration and describes the instant it is intended for.
Both currencies are ISO 4217 codes present in the declared table.
limitations: No FX retrieval, verification, interpolation or triangulation; no forward rates.
One rate per conversion, no spread or fee handling.
Single-currency engagements only: no consolidation or translation of statements.

inputs.name: amount
inputs.desc: the amount in the source currency

inputs.name: rate
inputs.desc: units of the target currency per one unit of the source currency (declared)

inputs.name: rate_date
inputs.desc: the rate date as YYYY-MM-DD (recorded, not verified)

inputs.name: rate_source
inputs.desc: where a sourced rate came from (recorded, not verified)

inputs.name: to_currency
inputs.desc: ISO 4217 code, e.g. EUR, CNY, JPY

defaults.question: Where the rate comes from
defaults.default_chosen: The owner declares it, with provenance user/sourced/assumption; a sourced rate must name its source. Nothing is retrieved or verified.
defaults.impact: A wrong or stale rate gives a wrong converted amount with no warning from the system.

defaults.question: Result currency
defaults.default_chosen: The converted amount is carried in the request's currency field, so set that field to the TARGET currency; the appendix states both codes.
defaults.impact: If the request currency is not the target, the displayed label is wrong even though the appendix is right.

label: Pricing rules
name: pricing_decision
intended_use: Cost-plus, target-margin, break-even and target-return prices from declared unit cost, fixed cost, volume and rate inputs.
unsupported_use: Researching willingness to pay or competitor prices; estimating a demand response; psychological pricing; discounts and promotions; tax.
assumptions: Unit cost and fixed cost are constant over the declared range.
The expected volume is the owner's declared figure.
limitations: No demand response, competitor price or price elasticity.
No discounts, VAT or other taxes.
A target-return price is arithmetic, not a recommendation.

inputs.name: expected_units
inputs.desc: units expected to be sold in the period

inputs.name: fixed_cost
inputs.desc: total fixed cost for the period, default 0

inputs.name: markup_rate
inputs.desc: markup on cost as a decimal, e.g. 0.60 for 60%

inputs.name: target_margin_rate
inputs.desc: optional margin on the price, greater than zero and below one

inputs.name: target_profit
inputs.desc: optional profit target for the period

defaults.question: Markup versus margin
defaults.default_chosen: The cost-plus price marks up the cost; the margin price divides the cost by one minus the declared margin. Both are shown separately.
defaults.impact: Treating a margin as a markup understates the price.

defaults.question: Volume
defaults.default_chosen: The declared expected units are used for the break-even and target-return prices.
defaults.impact: A different volume changes both prices.

label: Demand line and revenue-max price
name: demand_curve
intended_use: A straight line fitted to declared price-quantity observations, with the slope, R-squared, elasticity at the mean price and, when the slope is negative, the revenue-maximising price on the fitted line.
unsupported_use: Identifying demand; causal claims; omitting variables, simultaneity or measurement error; non-linear demand; market data retrieval; pricing recommendations.
assumptions: The pairs are comparable observations of the same market in the same period basis.
The relationship is approximately linear within the observed range.
limitations: No identification, omitted-variable or endogeneity correction.
Constant price or constant quantity blocks the fit.
The revenue-maximising price exists only for a negative fitted slope and only within the fitted line.

inputs.name: prices
inputs.desc: observed or declared prices, one per observation

inputs.name: quantities
inputs.desc: quantity demanded at each price, paired by position

defaults.question: Functional form
defaults.default_chosen: A straight line, quantity on price, fitted by least squares.
defaults.impact: A log or kinked form would give a different slope and elasticity.

defaults.question: Interpretation
defaults.default_chosen: An association between the observed pairs; the fit is not an identified demand curve.
defaults.impact: A price set from the fit may not hold when supply or income shifts.

label: Cost-benefit analysis
name: cost_benefit
intended_use: Discounted cost-benefit appraisal: present values of declared costs and benefits, the net present value and the benefit-cost ratio.
unsupported_use: Monetising non-monetised effects; choosing the discount rate; tax, financing or risk adjustment; probability distributions or Monte Carlo; distributive weighting.
assumptions: Costs and benefits are the owner's declared values on one basis.
The declared rate is the appropriate social or financial discount rate.
limitations: No monetisation of non-monetised effects, no risk adjustment and no distributional analysis.
One rate for all periods; no mid-period timing.
No tax or financing effects.

inputs.name: benefits
inputs.desc: benefit per period, same length as costs

inputs.name: costs
inputs.desc: cost per period, starting at period 1

defaults.question: Discounting
defaults.default_chosen: Costs and benefits are end-of-period from period 1 and discounted at the declared rate (default 0).
defaults.impact: A different rate or timing changes the net value and can change its sign.

defaults.question: What counts as a benefit
defaults.default_chosen: Only the monetised benefits the owner declared; no unmonetised effect is valued by the system.
defaults.impact: Omitting an effect understates the appraisal; valuing it is the owner's judgement.

label: Cost-effectiveness analysis
name: cost_effectiveness
intended_use: Cost-effectiveness analysis against a declared comparator: incremental cost per unit of effect (ICER) for each other option, with dominance flags.
unsupported_use: Comparing different outcome scales; weighting or aggregating several effects; probabilistic sensitivity analysis; deciding a willingness-to-pay threshold.
assumptions: Costs and effects are declared on one basis and one outcome scale.
The first option is the intended comparator.
limitations: One outcome scale only; no willingness-to-pay threshold and no sensitivity analysis.
An option with the same effect as the comparator has an undefined ratio and blocks.
Dominance is flagged, not ranked.

inputs.name: options
inputs.desc: the first option is the comparator; each other option is compared with it on cost and effect

defaults.question: Comparator
defaults.default_chosen: The first listed option is the comparator.
defaults.impact: A different comparator changes every incremental ratio.

defaults.question: Effect scale
defaults.default_chosen: All options state their effect on one declared scale.
defaults.impact: Mixing scales makes the ratios incomparable.

label: Social return on investment
name: sroi
intended_use: Social return on investment: present value of declared social benefits divided by the declared investment.
unsupported_use: Estimating or verifying social benefits; additionality, deadweight, attribution or displacement adjustments; assurance; comparing across different outcome scales.
assumptions: Benefits are declared values on one basis.
The investment is a declared amount and the rate is the owner's choice.
limitations: No additionality/attribution adjustment and no assurance; the result is a declared-input ratio.
One outcome aggregate only.
Sensitivity to the valuation assumptions is not computed.

inputs.name: benefits
inputs.desc: monetised benefit per period, starting at period 1

defaults.question: Benefit valuation
defaults.default_chosen: The benefits are the owner's declared monetised values; the system does not value a social outcome.
defaults.impact: The ratio is only as good as those valuations.

defaults.question: Adjustments
defaults.default_chosen: No deadweight, attribution, displacement or drop-off adjustment is applied.
defaults.impact: Real SROI practice may require them; here they must be supplied already adjusted if wanted.

label: Net present value
name: npv
intended_use: Value a stream of cash flows at a user-supplied discount rate.
unsupported_use: Choosing the discount rate; ranking mutually exclusive projects of unequal scale or life; unequal period lengths.
assumptions: Cash flows are certain given the inputs.
limitations: Single constant discount rate.

defaults.question: Timing and rate convention
defaults.default_chosen: Cash flows occur at period end; the first cash flow is at t=0 and is undiscounted; the rate is taken as given.
defaults.impact: Changes NPV if cash flows are mid-period or the rate is not the right hurdle.

label: DCF valuation (year-end)
name: dcf_valuation
intended_use: Discount a declared stream of free cash flows at a declared rate and declared timing (end-of-period, or an explicit mid-year convention), with an optional Gordon-growth terminal value, to an enterprise value.
unsupported_use: Forecasting the cash flows; choosing the discount rate or growth (declare them, or use wacc and your own inputs); tax computation; real-option or scenario valuation; equity value claims beyond the separate equity_bridge method.
assumptions: The cash flows and the discount rate are the owner's declared inputs.
The terminal growth rate persists forever and stays below the discount rate.
Under a mid-year convention every flow is assumed to arrive mid-period.
limitations: The result is model-conditional arithmetic, not a market price or a forecast guarantee.
The terminal value typically dominates the answer and rests on the growth assumption.
No tax computation; the enterprise-to-equity bridge is the separate equity_bridge method.

inputs.name: cashflows
inputs.desc: free cash flows, one per period, first in period 1

inputs.name: terminal_growth
inputs.desc: optional perpetual growth after the forecast; must be below the discount rate

inputs.name: timing
inputs.desc: discounting convention: 'end' (default, end-of-period) or 'mid' (mid-year, exponents t-0.5)

defaults.question: Terminal value
defaults.default_chosen: No terminal value unless terminal_growth is declared; then a Gordon-growth value on the last cash flow, discounted at the same rate and timing convention.
defaults.impact: Without a terminal value the valuation covers only the explicit forecast and will usually understate a going concern.

defaults.question: Timing and taxes
defaults.default_chosen: Cash flows are end-of-period, after tax and after claims as supplied; no tax is computed. Declare timing='mid' to discount every flow (and the terminal value) one half-period earlier.
defaults.impact: A mid-year convention raises the value; pre-tax cash flows with an after-tax discount rate are inconsistent.

label: Break-even point
name: breakeven
intended_use: Units needed to cover fixed cost at a constant unit contribution, with the break-even revenue, contribution margin, margin of safety and target-profit volume when those inputs are declared.
unsupported_use: Multi-product mix; step-fixed costs; non-linear price or cost; a demand response to the price; tax; financing cost.
assumptions: Linear cost and revenue.
The expected volume is the owner's declared input, not a forecast.
limitations: Single product; a mix needs multi_product_breakeven.
No tax, financing or working-capital effects.
The margin of safety is relative to the declared expected volume only.

inputs.name: expected_units
inputs.desc: optional expected sales volume, for the margin of safety

inputs.name: target_profit
inputs.desc: optional pre-tax profit target, for the required volume

defaults.question: Cost behavior
defaults.default_chosen: Fixed cost is constant and unit price and variable cost are constant.
defaults.impact: Break-even moves if costs are stepped or prices change with volume.

defaults.question: Margin of safety and target profit
defaults.default_chosen: Both are reported only when expected_units or target_profit is declared; neither is assumed.
defaults.impact: A different expected volume changes the margin of safety but not the break-even point.

label: Multi-product break-even
name: multi_product_breakeven
intended_use: Break-even in units and revenue for a fixed product mix: the mix-weighted contribution margin and the per-product break-even quantities.
unsupported_use: A changing mix, step costs, capacity limits, price-volume relationships or tax; forecasting which mix will actually occur.
assumptions: Each product's price and variable cost are constant.
The declared mix is the mix that will be sold.
Fixed costs do not change with volume.
limitations: One break-even point for one declared mix; no capacity limits or step costs.
No tax, financing or working-capital effects.
Per-product units are a break-even mix, not a target.

inputs.name: fixed_costs
inputs.desc: total fixed costs for the period

inputs.name: products
inputs.desc: two or more products with a declared mix (mix_units are the relative quantities sold)

defaults.question: Mix assumption
defaults.default_chosen: The declared mix_units are held constant and used as the weighting.
defaults.impact: A different mix changes the weighted contribution and the break-even.

defaults.question: Cost behaviour
defaults.default_chosen: Fixed costs are constant and unit prices and variable costs are constant over the range.
defaults.impact: Step costs or volume discounts break the single break-even point.

label: Unit economics
name: unit_economics
intended_use: Unit contribution margin, payback of the acquisition cost and (when a churn rate is declared) a period-value LTV and LTV/CAC.
unsupported_use: Estimating churn, retention curves or customer lifetime modelling; discounting LTV to present value; tax, financing or cross-sell; segment-level CAC.
assumptions: Prices, costs and churn are the owner's declared inputs.
The unit margin is earned each period until churn.
limitations: No present-value discounting, retention curve, tax or financing.
Churn is a single constant rate.
Segment or product-level CAC is not modelled.

inputs.name: churn_rate
inputs.desc: period churn in (0,1); if supplied, LTV = unit margin / churn

defaults.question: LTV definition
defaults.default_chosen: LTV = unit margin / declared churn rate (period value, no discounting); omitted when no churn is declared.
defaults.impact: A different LTV convention (e.g. discounted, cohort-based) would give a different number.

defaults.question: Payback
defaults.default_chosen: Payback periods = acquisition cost / unit margin.
defaults.impact: It assumes the margin is earned every period at the same rate.

label: Descriptive statistics
name: descriptive_stats
intended_use: Summarize one numeric variable in a dataset (n, missing, mean, median, range, sample SD).
unsupported_use: Inference (intervals, tests, effect sizes), weighted or clustered survey data, grouped summaries, quartiles.
assumptions: Observations are numeric and the listed codes fully identify missing values.
limitations: Descriptive claims only; no inference.
Float reference comparison tolerance is 1e-9 relative.

inputs.name: missing_codes
inputs.desc: user-defined missing codes such as 99; never read as values

inputs.name: values
inputs.desc: the observations; blank or null counts as missing

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: Blank, null and user-defined missing codes are excluded from every statistic (listwise for one variable) and counted.
defaults.impact: Including codes as values would distort every statistic.

defaults.question: Median and spread definitions
defaults.default_chosen: Median averages the two middle values for even n; variance and SD use n-1 (sample).
defaults.impact: Population SD (n) is smaller; packages differ on quartile definitions, which are not reported.

defaults.question: Small-sample threshold
defaults.default_chosen: Fewer than 30 valid observations triggers cautionary wording [PROVISIONAL].
defaults.impact: Changes only the wording, not the numbers.

label: Pearson correlation
name: pearson
intended_use: Linear association between two numeric variables in a sample, with interval, p-value and effect size.
unsupported_use: Causal claims; non-linear relationships; clustered, weighted or repeated-measures data; more than two variables.
assumptions: Pairs are independent observations.
Relationship is approximately linear.
Approximate normality, screened by skewness and kurtosis only.
limitations: Normality screen limits (2 and 7) are conventional placeholders [UNVERIFIED].
Linearity and independence are not tested.
Interval uses the Fisher z approximation.

inputs.name: missing_codes
inputs.desc: user-defined missing codes such as 99; apply to both variables

inputs.name: x
inputs.desc: first variable; blank or null counts as missing

inputs.name: y
inputs.desc: second variable, paired by position with x

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: A pair is excluded if either value is blank, null or a declared missing code (pairwise deletion for two variables).
defaults.impact: Counts of excluded pairs are reported; other handling (imputation) changes the estimate.

defaults.question: Multiple comparisons
defaults.default_chosen: One test, so no correction. If more tests are run, declare a correction in the spec.
defaults.impact: Running many correlations without correction inflates false positives.

defaults.question: Effect-size wording thresholds
defaults.default_chosen: Absolute r below 0.1 negligible, below 0.3 small, below 0.5 medium, otherwise large (Cohen-style conventions) [PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED]. The effect size is the coefficient itself.
defaults.impact: Changes only the descriptive word, not the numbers.

defaults.question: Precision statement
defaults.default_chosen: Precision is conveyed by the confidence interval; no separate power calculation is made.
defaults.impact: A wide interval signals low precision.

defaults.question: Assumption screen and fallback
defaults.default_chosen: If skewness or excess kurtosis of either variable exceeds the declared limits, switch to Spearman as a logged amendment.
defaults.impact: Spearman is robust to outliers and skew but measures monotone, not linear, association.

label: Linear regression
name: ols
intended_use: Linear association of one numeric outcome with up to five numeric predictors, with intervals, p-values and effect sizes.
unsupported_use: Causal claims; categorical predictors; interactions; non-linear fits; clustered, weighted or time-series data; prediction beyond the observed range.
assumptions: Observations are independent.
The outcome is approximately linear in the predictors.
Residual variance is constant (screened) or robust errors are used.
limitations: Linearity, independence, and the correct specification are not tested.
No interactions, transformations, categorical predictors, weights or clustering.
At most five predictors.
F-form Breusch-Pagan and the diagnostic limits are conventions [UNVERIFIED].

inputs.name: missing_codes
inputs.desc: user-defined missing codes; a row with any missing value is excluded

inputs.name: predictors
inputs.desc: name -> values for each predictor, paired by position with y (names: letters and underscores only)

inputs.name: y
inputs.desc: outcome variable; blank or null counts as missing

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: A row is excluded (listwise deletion) if the outcome or any predictor is blank, null or a declared missing code.
defaults.impact: Excluded rows are counted; imputation would change estimates and bias depends on the missingness mechanism.

defaults.question: Multiple comparisons
defaults.default_chosen: Coefficient p-values are reported unadjusted; no correction is applied.
defaults.impact: With many predictors some will look significant by chance; declare a correction in the spec if needed.

defaults.question: Effect-size wording thresholds
defaults.default_chosen: Cohen-style f-squared cut-offs 0.02, 0.15 and 0.35 for small, medium, large [PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED]. Standardized coefficients are also reported.
defaults.impact: Changes only the descriptive word.

defaults.question: Diagnostic screens
defaults.default_chosen: Residual skewness 2 and excess kurtosis 7 limits, F-form Breusch-Pagan level 0.05, largest VIF 10, largest Cook's distance 1 [PROVISIONAL, UNVERIFIED conventions]. Normality, collinearity or influence failures block; heteroskedasticity switches to HC3 robust errors as a logged amendment.
defaults.impact: Looser or stricter limits change which analyses are blocked.

defaults.question: Precision statement
defaults.default_chosen: Precision is conveyed by confidence intervals; no power calculation is made.
defaults.impact: Wide intervals signal low precision.

label: Welch two-sample t-test
name: welch_t
intended_use: Compare the means of two independent groups on a numeric outcome, with interval, p-value and standardized effect size.
unsupported_use: Paired or repeated measures; more than two groups; causal claims; clustered data; proportions or counts.
assumptions: Observations are independent within and between groups.
Group means are approximately normal (screened by skewness and kurtosis only).
limitations: Normality screen limits are conventions [UNVERIFIED].
Hedges g interval is a large-sample approximation.
Independence is not tested.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.desc: exactly two groups: name -> observations (letters and underscores in names; group sizes may differ)

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: Blank, null and declared missing codes are excluded within each group and counted.
defaults.impact: Excluded counts are reported.

defaults.question: Test choice
defaults.default_chosen: Welch's unequal-variance t-test (no equal-variance assumption), two-sided.
defaults.impact: Student's pooled t-test gives different degrees of freedom and p-values when variances or group sizes differ.

defaults.question: Standardized effect size
defaults.default_chosen: Hedges' g using the pooled standard deviation, with a large-sample normal interval [approximate]. Cohen-style cut-offs 0.2, 0.5, 0.8 [UNVERIFIED conventions].
defaults.impact: Using each group's SD (Glass) or the Welch-style average changes g.

defaults.question: Multiple comparisons
defaults.default_chosen: One test, so no correction.
defaults.impact: Several comparisons inflate false positives; declare a correction in the spec.

defaults.question: Assumption screen and fallback
defaults.default_chosen: If either group's skewness or excess kurtosis exceeds the declared limits, switch to the Mann-Whitney test as a logged amendment.
defaults.impact: Mann-Whitney compares rank distributions and reports a median-type shift, not a mean difference.

label: One-way ANOVA
name: anova
intended_use: Compare the means of three or more independent groups with an omnibus F test, an eta-squared effect size and per-group summaries.
unsupported_use: Repeated measures; two-way or factorial designs; post-hoc pairwise tests; causal claims; fewer than three groups.
assumptions: Observations are independent within and between groups.
Group distributions are approximately normal (screened by skewness and kurtosis only).
Group variances are approximately equal (screened by Levene's test).
limitations: Normality and Levene screen limits are conventional placeholders [UNVERIFIED].
Independence is not tested.
No post-hoc pairwise comparisons or repeated-measures designs.
Eta-squared is a sample effect size and is not bias-corrected.

inputs.name: groups
inputs.desc: three or more groups: name -> observations (letters and underscores in names; sizes may differ)

defaults.question: Missing-value handling
defaults.default_chosen: Blank, null and declared missing codes are excluded within each group and counted.
defaults.impact: Excluded counts are reported.

defaults.question: Test
defaults.default_chosen: One-way independent ANOVA (F test), two-sided, comparing group means.
defaults.impact: Repeated-measures, two-way and ANCOVA designs are not supported.

defaults.question: Effect size
defaults.default_chosen: Eta-squared (between-group SS over total SS), with Cohen-style cut-offs 0.01, 0.06, 0.14 [UNVERIFIED conventions].
defaults.impact: Omega-squared (less biased) is not reported.

defaults.question: Assumption screens and fallback
defaults.default_chosen: If any group's skewness or excess kurtosis exceeds the declared limits, or Levene's test for equal variances rejects at the declared level, switch to Kruskal-Wallis as a logged amendment.
defaults.impact: Kruskal-Wallis compares rank distributions, not means.

defaults.question: Multiple comparisons
defaults.default_chosen: The omnibus F test makes no pairwise comparisons, so no correction is applied.
defaults.impact: Post-hoc pairwise tests would need their own correction.

label: Chi-square association
name: chi_square
intended_use: Test whether two categorical variables are independent from a table of observed counts, with a Cramer's V effect size.
unsupported_use: Goodness of fit; ordered categories; repeated or paired counts; causal claims; tables with small expected counts (blocks).
assumptions: Observations are independent and each is counted in exactly one cell.
Expected counts are large enough (screened; at least 5).
limitations: The p-value is an approximation; exact tests are not implemented.
No Yates continuity correction for 2x2 tables.
Cramer's V cut-offs are coarse [UNVERIFIED].

inputs.name: table
inputs.desc: a table of non-negative whole-number counts (rows x columns)

defaults.question: Test
defaults.default_chosen: Pearson chi-square test of independence on a table of observed counts.
defaults.impact: Goodness-of-fit (one variable) and Fisher's exact test are not implemented.

defaults.question: Expected-count rule
defaults.default_chosen: If any expected count is below 5, the analysis blocks (fail-closed) instead of reporting an unreliable p-value.
defaults.impact: Small tables may block; larger samples or collapsing categories may be needed.

defaults.question: Effect size
defaults.default_chosen: Cramer's V, with coarse cut-offs 0.1, 0.3, 0.5 [UNVERIFIED conventions].
defaults.impact: The interpretation of V depends on the table dimensions.

label: Power and sample size
name: power_analysis
intended_use: Plan a two-sample or one-sample comparison of means: the power for a stated effect, and the minimum detectable effect at a declared target power, under the normal approximation.
unsupported_use: Exact power under the noncentral t distribution; proportions or counts; cluster, weighted or repeated-measures designs; multiplicity; treating a high power as a guarantee of significance.
assumptions: Observations are independent within and between groups.
The standard deviations supplied are the planning values and are positive.
A single test at the declared alpha, with the declared number of tails.
limitations: Normal approximation; no noncentral t exactness.
No clustering, weights or repeated measures.
Power describes the design, not the study's actual outcome.

inputs.name: design
inputs.desc: two_sample compares two means; one_sample tests a single mean

inputs.name: effect
inputs.desc: the difference (or mean) to detect, in the units of the outcome

inputs.name: n1
inputs.desc: sample size of group 1 (or the single sample for one_sample)

inputs.name: sd1
inputs.desc: standard deviation of group 1 (or the single sample)

inputs.name: target_power
inputs.desc: power used to compute the minimum detectable effect, default 0.8

defaults.question: Underlying distribution
defaults.default_chosen: The normal approximation. It is exact when the standard deviations are known or planned; with sds estimated from a pilot, exact power uses the noncentral t distribution.
defaults.impact: Exact power is somewhat lower than the normal approximation when sds are estimated.

defaults.question: Multiplicity
defaults.default_chosen: A single comparison is assumed; the correction does not account for several planned tests.
defaults.impact: A family of tests needs a smaller per-test alpha (see multiple_comparison).
